week_thesis: The S&P 500 has posted 6 consecutive winning weeks (now at 7,399) with Q1 2026 earnings season producing an 84% EPS beat rate and 27.7% blended growth — the strongest since Q2 2021. A key regime shift is underway: 'AI changing of the guard' per CNBC (May 8) as AI chip spending rotates from Nvidia to AMD, Intel, and Micron on data center CPU/GPU buildout. AI capex projected at $571B in 2026. Three catalysts align: (1) PLTR Q1 beat (85% revenue growth, US commercial +133%, FY guidance raised to 71% growth); (2) AMD data center momentum ($5.8B, +57% YoY, guided Q2 to $11.2B); (3) INTC secular turnaround (up 430% YoY, surpassed dotcom-era market cap, 5% off recent high). Macro backdrop is risk-on. Only earnings risk in universe this week is AMAT (May 14) — excluded.

buys.reasoning: Palantir reported Q1 2026 on May 4: revenue $1.63B (+85% YoY, beat $1.54B estimate), US commercial $595M (+133% YoY), US gov $687M (+84% YoY), net income quadrupled to $870.5M. Raised FY2026 guidance to $7.65-7.66B (+71% YoY vs $7.27B consensus). Q2 guide $1.8B vs $1.68B expected. Algo score 0.36 (3rd overall) with 11% dip from recent high = pullback entry. No earnings this week. Bullish retail + institutional sentiment on defense AI + AIP commercial platform.

AMD reported Q1 2026 on May 5: total revenue $10.3B (+38% YoY, beat), data center $5.8B (+57% YoY). Non-GAAP EPS $1.37 vs $1.18 expected. Q2 guidance $11.2B (+46% YoY). Stock soared 16% post-earnings. CNBC 'AI changing of guard' rotation (May 8). Up 66% YTD. No earnings risk this week.

Intel up 430% over past year, surpassed dotcom-era market cap (~$550B), +33% in early May, 13% single-day pop. Algo score 0.41 (2nd overall) with 5.26% pullback = ideal swing entry. 'Intel and Micron poised to break major milestones' (CNBC May 5). Foundry recovery + Gaudi AI accelerators + HBM positioning driving structural re-rating. No earnings this week.
